headline: Investors weighing Anthropic's planned stock-market debut are struggling to put a price on the risk that its AI could cause catastrophic harm, Bloomberg reports.
score_reason: Keeps the pool score: an analysis piece of real interest, built on opinions rather than new facts.
importance_line: Anyone who may buy Anthropic shares faces a risk nobody can measure, and the way it is handled could set a pattern for other AI listings; the views are opinions from investors and insurers, and Anthropic declined to comment.
summary: Bloomberg reports that investors considering Anthropic's planned stock-market listing, which could value it at up to $2 trillion, are struggling to price the risk that AI could cause catastrophic harm, after a public debate in which chief executive Dario Amodei published an essay on losing control of AI. Quoted investors and insurers disagree on how to measure it, and one venture capitalist proposed a $1 trillion escrow for AI labs; Anthropic declined to comment.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked; Bloomberg text read on Moneycontrol. Several views are opinions quoted by Bloomberg (Lessin, Moss, Ziolkowski), not findings.
